verdict.rationale: Gram documents building MCP servers that authenticate through an external OAuth 2.0 provider (Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, or a custom server). That implies tool calls run with an authenticated user's own OAuth credentials, and tool calls are tied to a named employee. The evidence does not describe a per-end-user connected-accounts store or per-user scoped token issuance for a platform's own customers; other permission scoping is per team, server and tool, not per end user. Missing for 10: explicit per-end-user connected-account management, per-user scoped token issuance and isolation, documentation of per-user upstream credential storage, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials

citations.quote: This guide shows you how to build an MCP server with external OAuth authentication.
you can use any OAuth 2.0 provider you have set up (such as Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, or your own OAuth server)
Every tool call in one exportable record, tied to a named employee
